title: When the Safehouse Wakes
premise: Kestrel Ashgrove, a whistle-blower living under four names in a government safe house, discovers the property has been listed for sale online — with interior photos that reveal his hiding place, his routines, and a coded message only his old handler could have planted. Ordered to extract Nadia Volkov, a Russian defector who may be bait for the mole who sold him out, Kestrel must choose between running and uncovering the truth. As he and Nadia evade hunters across three cities, he realizes she carries proof of the betrayal — and that falling for her was the one vulnerability his enemies counted on. In the end, Kestrel trades his own anonymity to expose the mole, choosing love and truth over the safety of a life built on lies.
about_author: Mirabel Delacroix is the pen name of a former intelligence analyst turned novelist who writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences. She lives off-grid by choice, which she insists is research, not paranoia.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet him mid-routine: checking sightlines, rotating identities, keeping the go-bag by the door. A late-night scroll through real estate listings reveals his safe house for sale — with photos of his kitchen, his bed, a sticky note bearing one of his aliases. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of a life built on vigilance.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He dissects the photos and finds metadata pointing to his former handler, Ruth Calloway, who went dark two years ago. His emergency contact at the agency stonewalls him, then offers a deal: extract defector Nadia Volkov from Prague, and they'll investigate the leak. Beat: fear curdles into suspicion — he's being handled again.

chapters.title: Prague, Rain, and a Stranger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In Prague he makes contact with Nadia, sharp-eyed and unimpressed, who immediately clocks his fake passport as agency-issue. She agrees to come only because her own handlers want her dead. Beat: wary mutual recognition between two people fluent in survival.

chapters.title: Extraction, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The extraction goes wrong — a sniper forces them off the planned route, and Kestrel realizes only three people knew the timing. They escape via freight yard, and Nadia reveals she has a drive containing files on an internal leak codenamed LANTERN. Beat: adrenaline giving way to dread; the trap is bigger than him.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knows
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. On a night train to Munich, Nadia recounts how LANTERN burned her network and why she suspects the mole sits high in the very office that sent Kestrel. She tests him with a half-truth about Ruth Calloway. Beat: intimacy born of interrogation — each measuring the other, both wanting to trust.

chapters.title: The House That Sold Itself
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. From a Munich safe flat, Kestrel traces the real estate listing to a shell company tied to Deputy Director Hale — the man who gave him the extraction order. He realizes the listing wasn't a leak; it was a lure to flush him out. Beat: cold clarity — he was never the rescuer, he was the package.

chapters.title: Safehouse of Glass
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Surrounded but not yet found, Kestrel and Nadia argue about the endgame: run forever or burn LANTERN down publicly. A near-miss with a hunter team forces them to shelter in a church crypt, where Kestrel admits he's tired of being no one. Beat: love declared quietly, in the space between danger and dawn.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ghost
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A dead-drop message from Ruth surfaces: she faked her death after discovering LANTERN and planted the listing herself — not to expose Kestrel, but to force him to move before Hale could erase him. She offers evidence if he can reach Berlin in thirty-six hours. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the mentor returns as a ghost with debts.

chapters.title: Berlin, Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Berlin meet is ambushed — Ruth is captured, and Kestrel learns Nadia's defection was partially engineered by Hale to draw out Ruth's evidence. Kestrel must decide whether Nadia is traitor or fellow prisoner. Beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth; every alliance now suspect.

chapters.title: When the Safehouse Wakes
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Nadia's POV. They broadcast LANTERN's files live during a press event Hale is attending, sacrificing Kestrel's last alias to do it. Hale falls; Ruth walks free; Kestrel, finally under his own name, chooses to stay visible beside Nadia rather than vanish again. Beat: resolution — belonging won at the price of safety, gladly paid.
